intro: Florianópolis is the capital of Santa Catarina in southern Brazil, a city spread over an island and a strip of the mainland facing it across a narrow bay. A reader sent us two of its trees: a massive twisted tree with plaques on its trunk on the waterfront of Ribeirão da Ilha, the old fishing village in the island's southwest, and a fig hung with aerial roots in Coqueiros, on the mainland side.
meta_description: Two trees in Florianópolis sent by a reader: a plaqued waterfront giant at Ribeirão da Ilha and a fig hung with aerial roots in Coqueiros.
question_meta: Two old trees in Florianópolis, Brazil, sent by a reader: a twisted giant on the shore of Ribeirão da Ilha and a fig of hanging roots in Coqueiros.
question_answer: The Plaque Tree on the Shore of Ribeirão da Ilha stands on a small paved point over the bay in the old fishing village of Ribeirão da Ilha, in the southwest of Santa Catarina Island. It is free to visit at any hour.
question_context: A reader sent us both of the Florianópolis trees on our map from their own walks, with a photograph of each. The first stands on the waterfront of Ribeirão da Ilha, a village settled by families from the Azores in the eighteenth century, whose painted houses and oyster farms still line the bay south of the city centre. Its trunk is dark, massive and twisted, two plaques are fixed to it, and its limbs run out almost level over the water beside a bench where people come to watch the sun go down behind the mainland hills. Its broad leaves look like those of a tropical almond, but we have not confirmed the species, and we do not yet know what the plaques say. The second is a fig in Coqueiros, on the mainland side of the bay, a knot of mossy stems under a dense crown from which curtains of thin aerial roots hang to the ground. We have no ages or measurements for either tree. If you know them, or can read the plaques, tell us on the tree's page and we will add what you send, with your words if you want them used.

faq.q: Where is the tree with plaques in Ribeirão da Ilha?
faq.a: On a small paved point on the waterfront at Rua Paulo Pedro Heidenreich, in the village of Ribeirão da Ilha, in the southwest of Santa Catarina Island. It is free to visit at any hour.
We do not know yet. Neither tree has a recorded age or girth. If you know one, tell us on the tree's page.

faq.q: Is there a fig to see in Coqueiros?
faq.a: Yes. A reader sent us a big fig hung with aerial roots near Rua Vereador José do Vale Pereira in Coqueiros, on the mainland side of the bay. We have not confirmed whether it stands on public ground, so look for it from the street.

trees.name: The Plaque Tree on the Shore of Ribeirão da Ilha

location.address: Waterfront at Rua Paulo Pedro Heidenreich, Ribeirão da Ilha, Florianópolis, Santa Catarina

trees.how_to_recognise: On a small paved point over the bay, beside a bench and a little blue building: a massive, twisted dark trunk with two plaques fixed to it, its limbs reaching out low over the water.
trees.access: Free. It stands on a paved public spot on the waterfront, open at all hours.
trees.story:
A reader sent us this tree from the shore of Ribeirão da Ilha, the old Azorean fishing village on the southwest coast of Santa Catarina Island, south of the centre of Florianópolis, and photographed it at dusk with the sun going down over the bay.

The picture explains why they stopped. On a small paved point between the road and the water, the trunk rises dark and enormous, twisting as it goes, and splits into limbs that run out almost level over the waves, one of them so long and low it looks ready to touch the surface. Someone has fixed two plaques to the trunk, and a man standing at its foot reaches only as high as where the bark begins to bulge. A bench and a little blue building keep it company, and the hills of the mainland line the far shore.

The broad leaves bunched at the tips of the twigs, a few turned red, are those of a tropical almond. A second photograph from the same reader, taken close to the trunk, shows one of the plaques, a strip of wood fixed to a great lichen-grey burl, the words burned into it by hand, "A árvore que fala", the tree that speaks. Who put it there, and what the other plaque says, we do not know. If you do, tell us here and we will add it.

Come at sunset, as the reader did.

trees.name: The Fig of the Hanging Roots in Coqueiros

location.address: Near Rua Vereador José do Vale Pereira, Coqueiros, Florianópolis, Santa Catarina

trees.how_to_recognise: A broad fig whose limbs spread from a knot of mossy grey stems, with curtains of thin aerial roots hanging from them down to the ground beside a low wall.
trees.access: The reader marked it near Rua Vereador José do Vale Pereira in Coqueiros. We have not confirmed whether it stands on public ground; look for it from the street.
trees.story:
"Fig," was all the reader wrote when they sent us this tree from Coqueiros, the neighbourhood on the mainland side of Florianópolis that looks back across the bay at the island and the old city.

Their photograph says the rest. It is taken from the foot of the tree, looking straight up, and the crown fills the frame from edge to edge. From a knot of grey stems, green with moss, the limbs climb and branch and branch again into a dense roof of small leathery leaves, and from everything hang curtains of thin aerial roots, dropping towards the ground the way a fig sends down new supports as it spreads. Some of them have already reached the earth and thickened, wrapping round the base like ropes. A low wall stands at its side.

We do not know which fig it is, how old, or how wide it spreads; many species are planted in Brazilian streets and squares. If you know this tree, tell us here and we will put your words on the page.

Stand under it and look up through the roots.

trees.name: The Fan Palm above the Horto Trail

location.address: Parque Ecológico do Córrego Grande (the old Horto Florestal), Florianópolis

trees.how_to_recognise: On the small paved trail that leaves beside the park's main little house, next to the playground, towards the upper car park: a palm with a rough reddish trunk whose crown of broad fans rises above the trees around it.
trees.access: Free, in a public park. Open in daytime.
trees.story:
"Esta palmeira fica em uma pequena trilha calçada que sai ao lado da casinha principal do horto," wrote the reader who sent us this palm from Florianópolis. It stands, they explain, on a small paved trail that leaves beside the main little house of the horto, next to the playground, heading for the upper car park.

Their photograph is taken from the foot of the trunk, looking straight up, and it shows why they stopped. The trunk is rough and reddish, wrapped in the fibres and old leaf bases a fan palm keeps as it grows, and it climbs clean through the younger forest around it. At the top the leaves open into wide, stiff fans, dark against the light, and the whole crown stands above the canopy of the trees beside it. Smaller palms crowd the undergrowth below, as if waiting their turn.

The reader calls it a palmeira leque, a fan palm. Which fan palm it is, and how old, we do not know yet; if you can tell from the leaves or the trunk, or know the park's records, tell us here.

Walk the trail from the playground and look up as the path climbs towards the car park.
